title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #20

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which twigs are best for making charcoal sticks? (1 mark)
   A. Green leaves
   B. Thick logs
   C. Dry, straight twigs about as thick as a pencil
   D. Wet, bent branches

2. Which tool is good for smudging charcoal? (1 mark)
   A. A finger or a tissue
   B. A stone
   C. A knife
   D. A wet brush of paint

3. When accompanying singers, the drummers should (1 mark)
   A. play as loud as possible
   B. play softly enough for the singers to be heard
   C. shout the words
   D. stop at every line

4. In a drawing of a drum with light from the left, which part is darkest? (1 mark)
   A. The side facing the light
   B. The side away from the light
   C. The white paper background always
   D. Nothing is dark

5. Which is a melodic percussion instrument? (1 mark)
   A. Cowbell
   B. Claves
   C. Kayamba
   D. Xylophone

6. On a xylophone, the long bars give (1 mark)
   A. no sound
   B. high notes
   C. low notes
   D. only clapping sounds

7. What do the letters WA stand for? (1 mark)
   A. Winning Arm
   B. Wing Attack
   C. Wing Ally
   D. Water Aim

8. Which position takes the centre pass to start the game? (1 mark)
   A. GD
   B. C, Centre
   C. GK
   D. GS

9. A value scale strip shows (1 mark)
   A. steps from light to dark of one colour
   B. a picture of a mountain
   C. only primary colours
   D. only black paint

10. Which colour is a secondary colour? (1 mark)
   A. Red
   B. Yellow
   C. Green
   D. Blue

11. Which is the first step in mixing green? (1 mark)
   A. Put red and black on the palette
   B. Put yellow and blue on the palette
   C. Use only white
   D. Use only water

12. How many claps are there in the pattern ta-te ta-te taa (rest)? (1 mark)
   A. Four
   B. Six
   C. Three
   D. Five

13. Variation in a melody means using (1 mark)
   A. no rhythm
   B. only rests
   C. only one syllable
   D. different syllables and note lengths

14. What makes ending on d good for a short melody? (1 mark)
   A. It sounds finished and at rest
   B. It is the highest note
   C. It is the loudest note
   D. It sounds unfinished

15. The shield and two crossed spears on the flag stand for (1 mark)
   A. music
   B. farming
   C. defence of freedom
   D. sports

16. A side roll is also called a (1 mark)
   A. frog roll
   B. star roll
   C. crab roll
   D. log roll

17. What is the last part of the sequence in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Running away
   B. Getting up slowly and standing tall
   C. Jumping
   D. Rolling backwards

18. A sequence in gymnastics is (1 mark)
   A. a set of movements performed in a fixed order
   B. a single balance
   C. a type of mat
   D. a rule break

19. Which is a way to give good feedback to a partner? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh at their mistakes
   B. Push them
   C. Say one thing that was good and one thing to improve
   D. Say nothing

20. In music, the sign p means (1 mark)
   A. soft
   B. fast
   C. stop
   D. loud

21. A patriotic song shows (1 mark)
   A. love for one's country
   B. love of sweets
   C. a rainy day
   D. fear

22. Which is used only for taking photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Radio
   B. Torch
   C. Digital camera
   D. Whistle

23. The centre of interest is (1 mark)
   A. the main thing you want people to notice
   B. the camera button
   C. the edge of the photo
   D. the middle of the room

24. Photography is (1 mark)
   A. painting with a brush
   B. singing songs
   C. the art of taking pictures with a camera
   D. cutting paper

25. To make the centre of interest clearer you can (1 mark)
   A. move very far away
   B. shake the camera
   C. add lots of clutter
   D. move closer to the subject

26. Music is written on a (1 mark)
   A. ruler
   B. staff
   C. wall
   D. table

27. How many finger holes are on the front of the descant recorder? (1 mark)
   A. Three
   B. Five
   C. Twelve
   D. Seven

28. A descant recorder is made of (1 mark)
   A. glass
   B. plastic or wood
   C. paper only
   D. metal foil only

29. Supine means (1 mark)
   A. curled
   B. face down
   C. face up
   D. standing

30. Floating means (1 mark)
   A. staying on top of the water without swimming
   B. swimming fast
   C. diving
   D. sinking

31. After entering, you should (1 mark)
   A. pull others in
   B. sit at the top
   C. stay at the edge
   D. move away from the edge so the next person can enter

32. What happens if you lift your head during a glide? (1 mark)
   A. You fly
   B. You go faster
   C. Your legs sink
   D. Nothing

33. When playing an animal game, you should play on (1 mark)
   A. soft, clear ground
   B. thorn bushes
   C. sharp stones
   D. broken glass

34. In the hawk and the chicks game, the chicks (1 mark)
   A. hold on gently behind the hen
   B. sing
   C. run away
   D. hit the hawk

35. Animal games are inspired by (1 mark)
   A. the movements and behaviour of animals
   B. clouds
   C. tall buildings
   D. cars

36. A working portfolio holds (1 mark)
   A. only finished prize work
   B. work in progress such as sketches and trials
   C. balls
   D. food

37. When someone comments on your work, you should (1 mark)
   A. argue
   B. walk away
   C. listen quietly and say thank you
   D. tear the work

38. How can you decorate a portfolio cover? (1 mark)
   A. By putting sand on it
   B. By pasting coloured paper or fabric
   C. By burning it
   D. By tearing it

39. Which are instrumentalists in a folk song? (1 mark)
   A. People playing drums or shakers
   B. The umpire
   C. Dancers only
   D. The audience

40. In a folk song, the soloist (1 mark)
   A. is the audience
   B. leads and sings the call
   C. is silent
   D. plays the drum only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. State three qualities of a good melody. (3 marks)

42. Give three warm-up activities before sprinting. (3 marks)

43. State three ways of showing fair play in a netball game. (3 marks)

44. Give three common mistakes in the crab balance and how to fix them. (3 marks)

45. Give four safety rules when making charcoal sticks. (4 marks)

46. Explain where the sun should be when you photograph a person and why. (3 marks)

47. What is the centre of interest in a photograph? (3 marks)

48. Explain how to make a tint of blue. (2 marks)

49. What does it mean to appreciate a work of Creative Arts? (2 marks)

50. Explain how to perform an animal game to a musical rhythm. (4 marks)

51. Why is swimming an essential life skill? (2 marks)

52. What does singing in unison mean? Why is it good for an anthem? (3 marks)

53. Describe how to play the note G on the descant recorder and explain how to get a good tone. (5 marks)

54. Why is it good to take different roles in animal games? (3 marks)

55. Why should a short melody end on d? (2 marks)

56. Explain the job of the drumhead and the shell of a drum. (3 marks)

57. Explain why animal games are called indigenous activities. (3 marks)

58. Explain why only the Goal Shooter and Goal Attack can score goals. (3 marks)

59. Why do we scratch and wet clay before joining pieces? (3 marks)

60. How should you receive feedback from others? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Dry, straight twigs about as thick as a pencil
   Dry, straight, thin twigs burn evenly into good drawing sticks.

2. A — A finger or a tissue
   A finger or tissue blends charcoal softly.

3. B — play softly enough for the singers to be heard
   Accompaniment supports the singers and must not cover their voices.

4. B — The side away from the light
   Shadows fall on the side away from the light, so it is darker.

5. D — Xylophone
   A xylophone has bars that give different notes, so it can play a tune.

6. C — low notes
   Longer bars vibrate more slowly and sound lower.

7. B — Wing Attack
   WA is the Wing Attack, who feeds the shooters.

8. B — C, Centre
   The Centre takes the centre pass.

9. A — steps from light to dark of one colour
   A scale strip shows one colour changing from light to dark.

10. C — Green
   Green is made from yellow and blue.

11. B — Put yellow and blue on the palette
   Green comes from yellow and blue.

12. D — Five
   Ta-te has two, ta-te has two, taa has one, and the rest has none, so five claps.

13. D — different syllables and note lengths
   Variation makes a tune interesting.

14. A — It sounds finished and at rest
   Ending on the home note gives a complete feeling.

15. C — defence of freedom
   The shield and spears represent the defence of freedom.

16. D — log roll
   Keeping the body straight like a log gives it the name log roll.

17. B — Getting up slowly and standing tall
   Finish by standing up slowly with control.

18. A — a set of movements performed in a fixed order
   A sequence links skills one after the other.

19. C — Say one thing that was good and one thing to improve
   Kind and helpful feedback includes praise and a suggestion.

20. A — soft
   The letter p stands for soft.

21. A — love for one's country
   Patriotic songs celebrate the nation.

22. C — Digital camera
   A digital camera is made for photography.

23. A — the main thing you want people to notice
   It draws the eye first.

24. C — the art of taking pictures with a camera
   A photograph is a picture taken by a camera.

25. D — move closer to the subject
   Getting closer helps the subject fill the picture.

26. B — staff
   The staff has five lines and four spaces.

27. D — Seven
   There are seven on the front and one thumb hole at the back.

28. B — plastic or wood
   Recorders are commonly made of plastic or wood.

29. C — face up
   Supine is lying on the back.

30. A — staying on top of the water without swimming
   Floating is resting on the surface.

31. D — move away from the edge so the next person can enter
   Make space for others.

32. C — Your legs sink
   Lifting the head lowers the legs.

33. A — soft, clear ground
   Soft, clear ground prevents injuries.

34. A — hold on gently behind the hen
   Chicks stay in line.

35. A — the movements and behaviour of animals
   Children copy how animals move.

36. B — work in progress such as sketches and trials
   It shows how work develops.

37. C — listen quietly and say thank you
   Good listeners grow.

38. B — By pasting coloured paper or fabric
   Decorating uses local resources.

39. A — People playing drums or shakers
   Instrumentalists play instruments.

40. B — leads and sings the call
   The soloist starts or leads.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stepwise motion, variation of syllables and note lengths, and ending on d.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Jogging, arm circles, leg swings, gentle stretching, short easy strides. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each activity.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Follow the rules; respect the umpire; shake hands with the other team; take turns in positions; encourage teammates. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hips sagging: push harder. Bent arms: straighten them. Head dropped: keep it in line.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake with a fix.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: An adult does the burning; keep far from the fire; leave the tin closed until cold; collect only dead twigs; wash hands afterwards. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rule.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Behind the photographer, so light falls on the front of the person. If the sun is behind the subject, the face is in shadow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the position, 2 marks for the reason.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: The main subject that you want the viewer to notice first, for example a friend's face or a flower.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for main subject, 1 mark for noticed first, 1 mark for an example.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Add white to blue, a little at a time, until it is as light as you want.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for white, 1 mark for adding gradually.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: To notice, understand and value it, giving reasons for what you think.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a game and a rhythm, clap or drum the beat, move to the beat, change the speed for different animals and add a song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps people stay safe near water and prevent drowning, and it keeps the body fit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone sings the same notes at the same time. It is simple and everybody can join in together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 2 marks for the reason.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: Hold the recorder with the left hand at the top and the right at the bottom. Cover the thumb hole and holes 1, 2 and 3 with the pads of the left fingers. Put the mouthpiece between the lips and blow gently and steadily with a soft too.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for holding, thumb hole, three holes, mouthpiece and gentle breath.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone gets a fair turn, learns to lead and follow, and the team works better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: d is the home note. Ending on it makes the melody sound finished.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each idea.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: The drumhead vibrates when struck and makes the sound. The hollow shell makes the sound fuller and louder.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the drumhead, 2 marks for the shell's job explained.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: They come from the communities and their environment, need little or no equipment and are learnt by watching and joining in.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Netball rules say only these two attackers may shoot, and only from inside the goal circle. Other players help by passing the ball to them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the two players, 1 mark for the goal circle, 1 mark for the role of the others.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: It makes the surface rough and sticky so the pieces hold together and do not fall off when dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for scratching, 1 mark for water, 1 mark for the reason.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen quietly, do not argue, say thank you and think about the ideas.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
